Subject: Redwoods connector — request to align on architecture and playtest

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. Our Product & Platform teams at Selene Systems are eager to validate the connector pattern you proposed so we can list Redwood in the Selene Marketplace. Before we sign the partner addendum we want to run a short architecture walkthrough and a 48-hour playtest against a staging tenant to verify routing, auth, and failure modes.

High-level asks:
- A short 60-minute architecture walkthrough (runtime, auth, fallback behavior)
- A smoke test plan (KV/prefix caching, batching, and rejection policy under concurrent sessions)
- A small test harness we can run from our CI to exercise model variants and timeouts

Would Marcus or someone from your integration team be available this week to walk through a proposed reference design? We can provide a staging account and some sample traffic.

Best,
Aisha

Aisha / Stephanie —

Thanks — confirmed for the walkthrough (joining now). I’m attaching the reference architecture diagram and the smoke test plan we’ll use as the canonical checklist during the session. Quick notes so the workshop is more efficient:

1) Reference design (attached selene_reference_arch.png) — highlights
   - Connector sits as an outbound client in Selene’s VPC; we support both mTLS and signed API-key flows.
   - Smart routing policy lives in our control plane; for partners we recommend a two-tier fallback: primary hosted model -> quantized local variant.
   - Prefix/KV caching allowed at the connector edge for repeated prefixes (opt-in).

2) Auth and credentials
   - We’ll issue a short-lived staging API key scoped to a single project and enforce token binding to IPs.
   - For production we recommend client-cert mTLS + HMAC signatures for request integrity.

3) Smoke test plan (attached connector_smoke_test_plan.docx) — tests included
   - Concurrency ramp: 1 -> 250 concurrent connections, measuring  p95 latency and token cost.
   - Cache-hit verification: send repeated prefix workloads and assert backend token consumption decreases by >40% over baseline.
   - Failure injection: simulate model OOM and ensure fallback to queued mode within 2s or error code 503 with Retry-After.
   - Auth rotation: rotate key during active session and validate zero-downtime for pinned sessions.

4) Test harness
   - Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/selene-connector (branch: playtest) — contains small Python harness and HTTP snippets (selene_multiplex_auth_example.http).

I’ll run through the diagram live. After the walkthrough I’ll push a test build and a sandbox key to the Confluence page you can access for 72h.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Marcus —

That was an excellent walkthrough; the diagram answered a lot of our questions. A couple of follow-ups from our eng team after the session:

1) Can the connector support TLS client authentication where the client cert is rotated daily by our cert manager? We want to avoid manual rotations.
2) For the cache-hit verification test — can you provide an explicit metric we should assert on our side (example: tokens_consumed/backend per minute) and a small grep-able log prefix so we can correlate events?
3) We need to confirm the exact error codes Redwood returns for throttling vs capacity; our infra will map those to user-facing messages.

We’ll start the playtest tomorrow morning. Please place the sandbox key in the Confluence page and grant Jonas read access to the repo.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Kapoor
Head of Platform Partnerships | Selene Systems

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwoods connector — request to align on architecture and playtest

Aisha —

Quick update after we pushed the sandbox key and short-lived creds to Confluence (link in related_links):

- Daily cert rotation: supported. We’ve added an automated cert-rotation hook in the connector (notes in selene_multiplex_auth_example.http). It will accept a cert chain signed by your cert-manager and rotate without dropping established sessions for pinned connections.
- Metric plumbing: we added a log prefix "redwood.selene.metrics" and a token_consumed metric in the harness (see repo README). For the smoke test assert: tokens_consumed/backend_per_minute drops by >= 40% between run A (cold cache) and run B (after 10 repeated prefixes).
- Error codes: 429 = rate_limit, 503 = backend_capacity, 500 = internal_error. We’ll push a small mapping table into the Confluence doc so your UX team can map messages.

Next steps / action items:
1) Selene runs the playtest tomorrow morning and uploads a brief results.csv to the Confluence page.
2) Redwood will run a targeted failure-injection job during Selene’s test window and collect traces.
3) If all criteria pass we’ll move to a marketplace onboarding checklist and legal will trigger the partner addendum.

I’ll ping once the failure-injection job is scheduled (ETA 4 hours into your window).

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Runtime Lead | Redwood Inference
